segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Chairman. Gentlemen, let's talk about the laws of physics for a second. Mr. Graves and Commander Fravor, I heard you talk about speed. When those objects broke the sound barrier, did they make a sonic boom?

segments.speaker: FravorDavid
segments.text: I was in a jet, you can't hear anything; it's kind of loud in there.

segments.speaker: GravesRyan
segments.text: Yeah, you're not able to actually personally tell within the vehicle. I will say the objects that we were seeing, they were spherical and they were observed up the Mach 2, which is a very non-aerodynamic shape.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: What about G forces? Let's talk about G forces of those vehicles. Could a human survive those G forces with known technology today?

segments.speaker: GravesRyan
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: FravorDavid
segments.text: No, not for the acceleration rates that we observed.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. What about what they look like? How close did you get? Did you see a seam or a rivet or a section? And what I mean is, obviously the jets you're flying have all those things. Did these objects have those?

segments.speaker: FravorDavid
segments.text: to Graves: Do you want to go ride?

segments.speaker: GravesRyan
segments.text: I didn't have the detail to be able to tell that.

segments.speaker: FravorDavid
segments.text: So we got within a half mile of Tic TAC, which people say that's pretty far, but in airplanes, that's actually relatively close. No, it was perfectly white, smooth, no windows. Although when we did take the original FLIR video that is out there, when you put it on a big screen, it actually had two little objects that came out of the bottom of it. But other than that, no windows, no seams, no nothing.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Mr. Grusch, as a result of your previous government work, have you met with people with direct knowledge or have direct knowledge yourself of non-human origin craft?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes, I personally interviewed those individuals.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Mr. Grusch, as a result of your previous government work, have you met with people with direct knowledge or have direct knowledge yourself about ATS advanced technologies that the US. Government has based on conventional advanced tech?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I was briefed to the preponderance of the Defense Department's, both space and aerospace compartment of programs.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Do you have knowledge or do you have reason to believe that there are programs in the advanced tech space that are unsanctioned?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes, I do.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. And when you say that they're above congressional oversight, what do you mean?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Complicated question. So there's some I would call it abuse here. So, congressional oversight of conventional special access programs. So I'll use title Ten. So DoD as an example. Right? So Ten. US. Code section 119 discusses congressional oversight of SAPS, discusses the depth sect's ability to waive congressional reporting. However, the Gang of Eight is at least supposed to be notified if a waived or waived bigoted, unacknowledged SAP is created. And that's public law...

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: I don't want to cut you off, but how does a program like that get funded?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I will give you generalities. I can get very specific in a closed session. But misappropriation of funds...

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Does that mean that there is money in the budget that is said to go to a program, but it doesn't, and it goes to something else?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes, I have specific knowledge of that.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Do you think US Corporations are overcharging for certain tech they're selling to the US Government and that additional money is going to programs?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Correct. Through something called Irad.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay, satellite imagery. Let's talk about satellite imagery. We have satellites all over the place. Some that we're aware of and many that we're not aware of. Right. We're taking pictures of everything at every point in second. Mr. Grusch, are you aware, do you have direct knowledge, or have you talked to people with direct knowledge that there are satellite imagery of these events.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: That was one of my primary tasks at Nga since we process, exploit, and disseminate that kind of information. I've seen multiple cases, some of which, to my understanding, and of course, I left Ng in April, so that's my information cutoff date. But I personally reviewed both what we call overhead collection and from other strategic and tactical platforms that were I could not even explain prosaically. And I have a degree in physics, by the way, as well. And I am aware that you guys have not seen these reports, unfortunately, and I don't know why.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Do you have direct knowledge? We've spoken people with direct knowledge that this imagery applies to crash sites, crash imagery?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I can't discuss that in an open session.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. Do you have any information that the US government is involved in a disinformation campaign to deny the existence of certain UAPs?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I can't go beyond what I've already stated publicly in my News Nation interview because it touches other sensitivities.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. I'll yield the balance of my time back. Thank you, Mr. Chairman.
